# A `Transaction` block naming exactly one `PaymentSplit`.
#
# The grouped spelling is for a payment made of several splits, but nothing
# stops a file naming one, and it is the case that reads differently inside:
# `payment_slots` gives a block naming one split a `None` slot, the same as a
# plain `txn_guid:` block, so it is paired by date/amount/memo rather than by
# the guid it names. Naming two, each slot carries its own guid and can only be
# matched by that split.
#
# It settles 60.00 of the 100.00 invoice — the first of the transaction's two
# receivable splits. The invoice is left part-paid on purpose: it is the state
# `a_payment_giving_two_settling_splits.txt` is read into to check that a
# second settling split can be added to a transaction that already settles
# this invoice.
#
# What this fixture produces: split 7081…5667 in the invoice's lot, the other
# receivable split untouched and in no lot, and the invoice owing 40.00.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
invoice "INV-USD-001"
  customer_id: "C-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-05
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-05
    description: "Consulting"
    action: "Hours"
    account: "Income:Sales"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
    tax_included: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-05
    due: 2026-02-05
    ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
    memo: "Invoice INV-USD-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-02-27
    amount: 60
    account: "Assets:Bank:USD"
    Transaction "5e6f708192a3b4c5d6e7f80912233445"
      PaymentSplit "708192a3b4c5d6e7f809122334455667"
